F5 model (one, chosen): a download is a copy of the user's own file on that device; it plays offline with no periodic online check-in while the file stays in the library and the account exists, including after a downgrade or a cancelled paid plan (the F7 over-quota rule). It is removed when the user removes the download or signs out of that device; when the file leaves the library (the user deletes it, the F7 over-quota policy deletes it after notice, or it is removed after a valid copyright notice); and after account deletion with notice. With no check-in, the device removes its copy at its next connection, so a device that stays offline keeps playing it until then; whether takedowns need a bounded check-in is an open question for /replica-architect and counsel. Single track, album, playlist or whole library. Available on every plan; the plan sets the number of download devices (caps front-loaded egress). After a downgrade or cancel above the new device cap, the user picks which devices keep downloads (default most recently used); the others remove their copies at next connection, after notice, within the F7 N-day window. If /replica-launch makes offline paid, switch fully to a lapse-after-grace model and drop keeps-playing wording. Parity for owners (the original's Local Files, YouTube Music uploads, Plexamp), so a feature line not a pitch; built after the waitlist gate. In-app purchase rules via /replica-launch. Replaces the note calling it the key paid feature.
